title: Red-Teaming for Generative AI: Silver Bullet or Security Theater?

bias_targets.methodology: Thematic analysis of public reports and real-world case studies of AI red-teaming exercises to evaluate how team composition (e.g., handpicked experts versus crowdworkers), expert selection, and resource availability introduce methodological biases into which AI risks are investigated.

Surveying existing red-teaming literature and benchmarks to critique the non-universality of values used for AI safety alignment, highlighting how current evaluations and definitions of 'harm' disproportionately reflect the norms of Western, English-speaking, or majority populations.

Reviewing contemporary red-teaming research to identify gaps in GenAI evaluation, specifically noting that current safety alignment and red-teaming efforts often fail to adequately test or support low-resource languages.
